title: 2021 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: The area of the region bounded by the graph of \[x^2+y^2 = 3|x-y| + 3|x+y|\] is \(m+n\pi,\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are integers. What is \(m + n?\)

solutions.text:
Consider the four sign cases for \(x-y\) and \(x+y.\) In one case, for example, \(|x-y|=x-y\) and \(|x+y|=x+y,\) so

\[ \begin{gathered} x^2+y^2=6x \\ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad (x-3)^2+y^2=9. \end{gathered} \]

The other three cases similarly give circles of radius \(3\) centered at \((0,3),\) \((-3,0),\) and \((0,-3).\) The relevant arcs form the boundary shown by these four congruent circle pieces.

The region consists of a central square of side length \(6,\) together with four semicircles of radius \(3.\) The square contributes area \(36,\) and the four semicircles have the area of two full radius-\(3\) circles, namely \(18\pi.\)

Therefore the area is \(36+18\pi,\) so \(m+n=36+18=54.\)

Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Split the graph by the signs of \(x-y\) and \(x+y\)
The four cases give semicircle arcs around a central square
